response: Yes, β-catenin is believed to have a role in the pathogenesis of sebaceous cell carcinoma of the eyelid. Research has shown that cytoplasmic overexpression of β-catenin is observed in the majority of cases of sebaceous cell carcinoma of the eyelid, and this correlates significantly with tumor size. It is hypothesized that β-catenin overexpression in sebaceous cell carcinoma of the eyelid may be a result of Wnt/β-catenin pathway dysregulation. However, further exploration is needed to fully understand its role in both the development and prognosis of sebaceous cell carcinoma of the eyelid.
